chunks: (David) said: "He is unjust in demanding your ewe to add to his (many) ewes. Many partners are surely -- unjust to one another, except those who believe and do the right; but there are only a few of them." It occurred to David that he was being tried by Us, and he begged his Lord to forgive him, and fell down in homage and repented.

key_terms.يَبْغِي: he acts unjustly or exceeds bounds

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Prophet David's judgment and repentance in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this narrative illustrates the concept of *Istidraj* or divine testing for Prophets, where David’s initial judgment in the case of the sheep (*Na'aj*) serves as a lesson in humility rather than error. The phrase 'except those who believe and do righteous deeds' is often interpreted to highlight the rarity of true spiritual perfection even among the righteous. This event underscores the necessity of constant self-reflection and immediate return (*Tawbah*) to God upon receiving divine insight.
